page: Microsoft Azure M128ms is a memory-optimized virtual machine engineered for enterprise workloads requiring extensive physical memory capacity. Powered by Intel Xeon 8280M processors running at a base clock frequency of 2.7 GHz on an x86_64 architecture, this instance supplies 128 vCPUs derived from 64 dedicated physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Memory capacity is substantial at 3,892.0 GB of RAM, yielding roughly 30.41 GB per vCPU. The instance bundles 4,398 GB of local SSD storage, while graphics processing units are absent.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate distinct architectural tradeoffs between single-thread execution and aggregated parallel throughput. The system achieves a top-tier result in large-block uncached memory read bandwidth (375.19 GB/sec) and strong performance in multi-threaded workloads, including stress-ng multi-core execution (87,468.65), multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (332.35 GB/sec), and Redis SET operations (79.29 million ops/sec). Conversely, single-threaded metrics such as single-core Geekbench (889.0), stress-ng single-core (1,038.58), and text generation speeds rank in the bottom decile, reflecting modest per-core clock performance compared to newer microarchitectures.

Cost efficiency is heavily concentrated in its density of RAM rather than per-core compute performance. Allocating nearly 4 TB of system memory and 4.4 TB of attached local SSD storage in a single virtual machine minimizes the operational overhead of managing distributed caching layers or multi-node relational clusters. However, utilizing this instance for thread-bound tasks or lightweight compute profiles leads to poor cost-to-performance efficiency due to the underutilization of its specialized memory subsystem.

Azure M128ms is best suited for memory-intensive enterprise environments, including massive in-memory databases like SAP HANA, large-scale Redis or Memcached clusters, data warehousing, and heavy extract-transform-load (ETL) processing pipelines requiring vast working memory pools.
description: Microsoft Azure M128ms is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 128 vCPUs across 64 physical cores powered by Intel Xeon 8280M processors operating at 2.7 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture and managed by Microsoft Hyper-V, the system delivers 3,892.0 GB of RAM (30.41 GB per core) and includes 4,398 GB of local SSD storage without dedicated GPUs. Benchmark evaluations show top-tier large-block memory read bandwidth of 375.19 GB/sec alongside strong multi-core throughput in stress-ng and Redis operations exceeding 79 million ops/sec. However, single-core benchmarks and serial tasks exhibit lower baseline performance. Hardware efficiency is optimized for scale-up memory footprints rather than raw compute velocity, making it suitable for in-memory databases, large Redis caching fleets, and massive relational database systems.
